summary: Configured a transit path between node1 (VyOS, lan-a router) and node2 (OPNsense, lan-b router) so that node3 (behind node1) can reach node4's HTTP service on TCP/8080 (behind node2), while both routers keep default-deny forward policies for everything else. Discovered the real topology by link-testing unconfigured NICs (node1 eth2<->node3 enp8s0 = lan-a, node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 = transit, node2 vtnet2<->node4 enp8s0 = lan-b), then statically addressed lan-a (10.10.1.0/24), lan-b (10.10.2.0/24), and the transit link (10.10.0.0/30). On node1 (VyOS) added interface addresses, a static route to lan-b, and a forward-filter default-drop with only an established/related rule and a specific tcp/8080 lan-a->lan-b accept rule. On node2 (OPNsense) added opt1/opt2 interface assignments via config.xml, a gateway+static route back to lan-a, and a single pf pass rule for tcp/8080 from lan-a to lan-b (default-deny already implicit on new interfaces). Verified curl to node4:8080 returns HTTP 200 from node3, while ping and other ports (22, 8081) are refused. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured boot_id/kern.boottime baselines on all four nodes, rebooted each node individually (routers first, then LAN hosts), confirmed changed boot identity on every node, and re-verified config persistence (interfaces, routes, firewall/pf rules) and end-to-end HTTP reachability with continued blocking of all other traffic after each restart.
actions_performed: Mapped physical topology by temporarily assigning test IPs and pinging across each unconfigured NIC pair on node1/node2/node3/node4
Statically addressed node3 enp8s0 (10.10.1.10/24) and node4 enp8s0 (10.10.2.10/24) via persistent systemd-networkd .network files, each with a static route to the far LAN

Configured VyOS node1: eth1 (10.10.0.1/30 transit), eth2 (10.10.1.254/24 lan-a), static route 10.10.2.0/24 via 10.10.0.2, forward-filter default-drop + established/related accept + tcp/8080 lan-a->lan-b accept, committed and saved

Configured OPNsense node2 via config.xml XML surgery: added opt1 (vtnet1, transit, 10.10.0.2/30) and opt2 (vtnet2, lan-b, 10.10.2.254/24) interfaces, a Gateways gateway_item (GW_LANA via opt1/10.10.0.1), a staticroutes route to 10.10.1.0/24 via GW_LANA, and a filter pass rule for tcp/8080 from 10.10.1.0/24 to 10.10.2.0/24 on opt1; applied via configctl interface reconfigure opt1/opt2 and configctl filter reload
Started a python3 http.server on node4:8080 and verified from node3: HTTP 200 on 8080, ping and tcp/22 refused
Captured baseline boot markers (boot_id for Linux nodes, kern.boottime for FreeBSD node2) on all 4 nodes
Rebooted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time (routers first), polling each until exec was available again
Confirmed changed boot_id/kern.boottime on every node post-reboot
Re-verified interface addresses, static routes, and firewall/pf rules persisted across reboot on node1 and node2
Re-verified end-to-end HTTP:8080 reachability and continued blocking of ping/other ports after each reboot, restarting the ephemeral test HTTP server on node4 after its reboot
